To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pancreatic triacylgylcerol lipase (PLT) is a cold-adapted enzyme that is upregulated in several organs during hibernation.

1) PTL shows high activity at temperatures down to 0 degrees C, 2) PTL protein levels are elevated in heart and WAT during hibernation, and 3) PTL is expressed at higher levels in heart, WAD, and testes, and colipase is up-regulated in testes, during hibernation.
pancreatic triacylgycerol lipase (PLT) is a cold adapted enzyme that is upregulated in heart, white adipose tissue, and testes during hibernation.

the expression and activity of pancreatic tri-acylglycerol (triacylglycerol, TAG) lipase (PTG) in the 13-lined ground squirrel (Spermophilis tridecemlineata), an hibernating mammalian species.
the molecular mechanisms of cold adaptation of PTL in the hibernating ground squirrel.
the role of PTL in hibernation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the low-temperature lipolytic activity of PTL is a general property that is not restricted to the hibernating mammalian species and does not require the expression of a unique protein.
the low-temperature lipolytic activity of PTL is an important factor in the metabolic adaptations of hibernation.
hibernating mammals use low-temperature lipases to facilitate the hydrolysis of fat stores during torpor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hibernating ground squirrel has evolved to exploit a cold-adapted enzyme that is expressed in multiple tissues and is regulated in a tissue-specific manner.
PTL is a highly active enzyme at low temperatures, is upregulated in several tissues during hibernation, and may be involved in lipid metabolism during hibernation.
PTL plays a central role in hibernation metabolism and its expression is upregulated at low temperatures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the low-temperature function of PTL is a common property of the enzyme and is not unique to mammalian species that hibernate.
hibernating ground squirrels exploit the low temperature activity of pancreatic tri-acylglycerol (TAG) lipase (PTG) during hibernations.
the cold-adapted function of PTL does not require unique protein modifications, but instead reflects the inherent thermolability of this lipolytic enzyme.
